rationale_bullets: A two-transfer battle: Chiles (63.4 PFF/261 at MSU -> 64.4; near-five-star in 2023, 20 career starts, 3,807 @ 61% with 24-14 + 452 rush; benched late 2025 but with a 10-3 late ratio - 'still graded as a Top 15 transfer quarterback' - P6) vs Marchiol (69.9/120 at WVU, B12 +6 -> 75.9; 7 career starts).

The scheme is the elevator: Chip Kelly's offenses (Oregon/UCLA/OSU 2024 title) consistently outperform their inputs, and Kelly RECRUITED Chiles at UCLA (Athlon); both QBs bring the dual-threat profile the system requires.
The 2025 baseline was below average (57/68 P4 adjusted - P6) with Stone (68.4/430, yr4) now gone; 'a transfer has opened the season as starter every year here since 2019' (PS).
Braun (attributed): 'they have 3 guys they can win with and the room is much deeper.'
52, M = two mid tapes + an unresolved battle + a real system prior - a coin-flip room with a competent floor.

rationale_bullets: Komolafe returns off a proven year: 75.9 PFF/189 att; 941 @ 5.0 with 11 TD and All-B10 honors; four 100-yard games after C.Porter's injury.
The depth is real: Himon (78.7/99; 486 @ 4.9), Sawchuk (74.8/109 at FSU, ACC +5 -> 79.8; 1,600 career yds at OU/FSU), Preckel short-yardage, M.Porter (BG).
Kelly's pattern (P6): a shared backfield (Henderson/Judkins at OSU) - and 'Kelly has never failed to produce an effective, productive run game.'
PS: 'my #26 RB corps.' C.Porter's career ends (yr4, second season-ending injury).
Weighted aggregate ~76.5 (~p48) + breadth + scheme floor = 58, M.

The duo is the case: Wilde (79.8 PFF/366 routes -> 78.8; 71/880/8 - 3rd-team All-B10, the school's best receiving season since 2016) + Eligon (74.5/285 -> 73.5; 521 @ 14.1 with over half in the final three games - the vertical complement).

The named caveat is Braun's own: 'The mid-tier of that wide receiver room is going to have to elevate' - Ahumaraeze (64.1/147), Wagner (64.8/113), Covey behind; Top150 4* FR McDuffie joins the two-deep (P6).
TE flipped: all-league Welcing (61.0/203) to Ohio State; in come blocker Honig (69.1/113 at UConn) and D2 All-American Dehnicke - Athlon is 'bullish,' the tape is neutral.
No transfer WRs taken (Athlon) - the bet is returning development inside Kelly's tempo.
Weighted aggregate ~73.4 (~p88) is duo-driven; mid-tier and TE hold it at 64, M.

The 2025 line was the program's best in years - PBLK 93p / RBLK 86p, Push #133 -> #71, pass pro #60 -> #27, 17 sacks (P6/PS) - and FOUR starters left, including both draft picks (Beerntsen 79.3/832, rd-7 BAL; Tiernan 70.5/835, rd-3 MIN) plus Carsello (78.1/840) and Lewis (64.2/638).
Oratokhai (72.3/835 -> 71.3) is the lone returning starter - 'the top guy' (PS) with G/C flex.

The imports: Seagren (63.7/713 at OkSt, B12 +8 -> 71.7 - 'a proven starter... the biggest addition' - Athlon), Anugwom (Alabama - zero volume, 'unknown' per P6), Anchondo (D2). Career starts drop to 43 (PS); 'they signed zero four-star linemen' (P6).
The counterweight: Kelly's system + Drevno; 'Kelly has never failed to produce an effective, productive run game' (P6).
Two real tapes + unknowns + a proven-scheme prior = 46, M.
Kilbane is the anchor: 84.0 PFF/491 (B10 +10 -> 94.0) - the second-best DL tape in this B10 round behind Michigan's Daley; 7.5 TFL, 3.5 sk (Athlon).

The entire rest of the starting front left: Hubbard (74.5/355; 20.5 career sacks - 5th all-time at NU), Saka (72.7/347) to Texas A&M ('their future first-rounder was poached' - P6), both DTs Bastone (70.5/455) + Story (68.5/401).

The interior is the stated problem: Flakes (59.7/374 -> 69.7) with 'questions... around him' (Athlon); adds are J.Johnson (68.5/255 at UCF -> 71.5), Kirks (OSU, no volume), FCS Stephen-Wangboje, FR Mayne. PS: 'they need some guys to develop on the interior.'
Context: RDEF 33p last year WITH the departed front; the PRSH 81p leaves with Hubbard/Saka.
Mechanical aggregate ~75 (~p74) is one-player-driven; 52, M = an elite edge over a bottom-third interior.
Brus returns at volume: 61.7 PFF/740 (-> 77.7 with the +16); 81 tackles in his first starting season; 'one of the most talented LBs' (PS).
The leader leaves: Uihlein (70.4/736 - 2nd-team All-B10; 100 tackles, 4 INT).

The replacement is a pedigree import: McKinzie (61.6/331 at Oklahoma, SEC +14 -> 75.6; 8 starts; 4* transfer grade; 'should start in Uihlein's spot' - P6). Glover (79.0 on 7 snaps; PS#56) is the high-ceiling depth question.
PS: 'they should remain strong.' LB caution: the raw tapes are 61-62; the offsets do the flattering.
52, M = average: one proven-volume returner, one pedigree import, thin behind.

Three stars return: Fitzgerald (77.9 PFF/725 -> 83.9 - all-league, #1 tackler), Turner (79.0/593 -> 85.0 - the Star/nickel), Fussell (62.5/504 -> 68.5; 16 career starts). Athlon: 'one of the Big Ten's best secondaries'; Braun (via PS): 'the best the back half has looked in years.'
The subtraction helps: Wallace (55.0/630 - the worst full-volume tape, yr4) leaves; ledger correction - F.Davis II (65.7/550) RETURNS per feed as unprinted rotation depth.
IN: Deasfernandes (73.1/631 at CMU, MAC -3 -> 70.1), Pate (Weber St). Walters (57.2/50) health is 'key' at field safety (Athlon).
Context: COV 40p as-played and PDR #73 temper the names; P6: 'above average... on returning production alone.'
Weighted aggregate ~77.3 (~p85) - two-star-driven; CB2/FS projection lands it 68, M.
ST rule: start at the 28th-percentile prior SPEC (STR #95 - PS) and adjust for personnel: BOTH legs are new - K Olsen -> Miami, P Akers (45.4/39.9) expired.
The replacements are credible: Kleather (Bowling Green; 27-31 over two seasons) and rFr Dugandzic - PS's #5-ranked PUNTER - plus LS Boutorwick (Michigan) and a dedicated ST assistant.
PS's own read: 'they will be better than expected and should make a climb in the STR despite losing their K and P.'
40, M = up from the base on credible legs + coordinator focus, capped by zero P4 kicking volume.
